exam.q: An owner says spreadsheets are free because there is no licence cost. Which response best reflects this course?
opts: Spreadsheets are always the cheapest option
The real cost sits in staff time spent re-keying, searching, fixing errors and chasing, which can be estimated and annualized
Spreadsheets should be banned in all businesses
Licence cost is the only cost that matters
exam.why: Hidden costs come from staff time spread across many small tasks; estimating hours and multiplying by loaded cost reveals them.

exam.q: A business enters timesheets in a mobile app, but payroll staff retype the hours into the payroll system. What is the next logical step?
opts: Return to paper timesheets
Add a second app for timesheets
Connect the time app to payroll so approved hours flow automatically
Ask staff to email their hours as well
exam.why: The data is already digital; connecting systems removes the re-keying step.

exam.q: In a maturity snapshot, finance scores 4 while operations and HR score 2. What does this most likely suggest?
opts: The next investment may deliver more in operations and HR
Finance needs a new ERP immediately
The scores should be averaged and ignored
Only finance matters for automation
exam.why: The weakest functions often limit the whole business and usually hold the next best opportunities.

exam.q: A clinic wants to stop retyping patient intake forms. Which solution addresses the problem at the source?
opts: Scanning paper forms into a folder
Hiring an extra receptionist
A larger filing cabinet
A digital intake form with required fields that sends data directly to the practice system
exam.why: Capturing data once, digitally, at the source removes retyping and illegible handwriting, while privacy controls protect the information.

exam.q: An accounting system's bank rules are set to auto-apply and have started miscoding fuel purchases as office supplies. What practice would have prevented this?
opts: Turning off bank feeds
Starting rules in suggest mode and reviewing them before switching to auto-apply
Coding everything to a single account
Reconciling once a year
exam.why: Suggest mode lets you confirm a rule's accuracy before it posts transactions automatically.

exam.q: A distributor's sales team often promises stock that is already committed to other orders. Which ERP feature addresses this?
opts: Automatic costing
Barcode labels on shelves
Available-to-promise showing on-hand and committed stock
A monthly stock report
exam.why: Available-to-promise shows what can actually be sold after existing commitments.

exam.q: A field technician completes a job, and the office must type the job notes into accounting to invoice. Which tool family removes this step?
opts: A field service app that syncs completed jobs to create draft invoices
A shared email inbox
A larger accounting team
A social media scheduler
exam.why: Field service apps capture job details on site and pass completed work to invoicing without retyping.

exam.q: A web store and a warehouse system both have APIs but no ready-made connector. What is usually the best first choice to connect them?
opts: RPA that clicks through both screens
Manual export and import each morning
Replacing both systems
An integration platform flow using their APIs
exam.why: When both systems have APIs, an integration platform is usually more reliable and cheaper than RPA or replacement.

exam.q: Which practice best reduces the risk of a broken integration going unnoticed for weeks?
opts: Building integrations with a personal login
Failure alerts and a named owner recorded in an integration register
Checking integrations once a year
Avoiding integrations altogether
exam.why: Alerts and a named owner make sure failures are spotted and fixed quickly.

exam.q: A manager wants a dashboard but cannot say which decisions it should support. What should come first?
opts: Buy the most advanced BI tool available
Add as many measures as possible
List the weekly decisions managers make and the one or two measures that inform each
Copy another company's dashboard
exam.why: Starting from decisions keeps dashboards focused and useful.

exam.q: During a finance review, which baseline is most relevant for an e-invoicing and payment-reminder opportunity?
opts: Days sales outstanding
Number of desks in the office
Website visitors per month
Number of suppliers
exam.why: E-invoicing aims to speed up collection, which days sales outstanding measures directly.

exam.q: A home-care organization finds that caregiver first-aid certifications sometimes lapse. Which opportunity addresses this?
opts: A larger payroll team
A certification register with automatic reminders before expiry
Annual performance reviews
A new website
exam.why: Automated renewal reminders tied to a certification register prevent lapses.

exam.q: An opportunity scores value 2 and effort 4 on the prioritization matrix. How should it usually be treated?
opts: As a quick win
As a strategic project
As a fill-in
Dropped or redesigned
exam.why: Low value and high effort places it in the avoid or rethink quadrant.

exam.q: A company is about to migrate 6,000 item records into a new ERP. What should it do first?
opts: Migrate everything as-is and clean up later
Profile the data, archive inactive items, merge duplicates and name an owner
Let each user fix records after go-live
Delete all records and start from scratch
exam.why: Cleaning master data before migration prevents spreading errors into the new system, and an owner keeps it clean.

exam.q: Which combination best represents the security basics for an SME adding new cloud tools?
opts: MFA, a password manager, least-privilege access and tested backups
A strong firewall only
Annual password changes and shared admin accounts
Relying on the cloud vendor for everything
exam.why: These controls address the most common ways small organizations are compromised or lose data.

exam.q: Two vendors give impressive but different demos. How can the business compare them fairly?
opts: Pick the one with the best presentation
Pick the cheapest subscription
Ask both to run the same scripted scenarios from your business and score them
Choose the vendor with the most features
exam.why: Scripted demos using your own scenarios give a like-for-like comparison of how each tool handles your work.

exam.q: A plan assumes a government program will pay for half of an ERP project, but the application has not been made. What is the main problem?
opts: Programs never support technology
The plan depends on funding that has not been secured and should be viable without it
ERP projects are always fully funded
Funding should never be mentioned in a plan
exam.why: Programs may be worth checking, but eligibility and availability change, so a plan should not depend on unsecured funding.

exam.q: Staff keep using an old spreadsheet after a new system goes live, even though they have been trained. Which action is most effective?
opts: Run the same training again
Delay the project
Buy a different system
Set a retirement date for the spreadsheet, support users through super-users and recognize use of the new system
exam.why: Reinforcement, retiring the old way and providing support, is what makes new behaviour stick.

exam.q: Three months after go-live, a bill capture tool shows fewer hours saved than expected. Adoption data shows a third of bills still arrive on paper. What is the best next step?
opts: Work with those suppliers to send bills by email to the capture address
Cancel the tool
Change the KPI to something easier to meet
Ignore the paper bills
exam.why: The gap is an adoption issue; moving the remaining bills to the new path is the direct fix.

exam.q: Which roadmap order best follows the course's guidance for an SME with no MFA, messy customer data and a planned CRM?
opts: CRM first, then data clean-up, then MFA
MFA and backups first, then customer data clean-up, then CRM
All three in the same month
Data clean-up only, with no CRM
exam.why: Security basics come first, and enabling data clean-up should precede the CRM that depends on it.
